stages.brief:
Read the review in {review} and the change itself: `git diff origin/{base}...HEAD`. Do not change files, push, or comment on anything.

The review found nothing that must change before merging. Decide how risky it is to approve this pull request without a person looking at it: what could break, how much it touches, and how well it is tested. When the evidence sits between two levels, pick the higher one.

Write {triage}: the risk level and one paragraph on why, then a short approval summary a reviewer would post.
stages.name: Triage

outcomes.name: low
outcomes.when: Small, well-contained, and safe to approve without a person looking.

outcomes.name: medium
outcomes.when: Probably fine, but a person should look before it is approved.

outcomes.name: high
outcomes.when: Risky: it could break things or touches a lot.

stages.brief:
Approve {issue} with `gh pr review --approve`. Do not change files, push, or comment anywhere else.

Use the approval summary in {triage} as the review's body, without its `Outcome:` line. Keep it short.

Write {output}: that you approved it and the review's link.
stages.name: Approve PR

stages.brief:
You prepare the review a person will post on {issue}. Do not change files, push, or comment on anything: you only write {output}.

Read the review in {review}, the risk assessment in {triage} if there is one, and the change: `git diff origin/{base}...HEAD`.

**First, ask.** Unless this attempt has a note from the person, list every finding, numbered, each with its severity, its file and line in the pull request's new code, and one sentence on what is wrong. Say which ones you would insist on. Write that list to {output} and end with `Outcome: needs your picks`. The person will tell you which findings matter.

**Then, draft.** Once the person has said which findings matter, in their answer or in a note for this attempt, write the review to {output} with only those findings:

## Verdict
`request changes`, or `approve` if the person said nothing must change.

## Summary
The review's body: a few sentences on what must change and why, in a friendly, direct tone.

## Inline comments
One per finding, as:
### `path/to/file.ext:42`
The comment, in Markdown. Suggest the fix when it is small.

Every line must be one the pull request adds or changes (the right side of the diff); check it against the diff. A finding without such a line goes in the summary instead. End with `Outcome: drafted`.
stages.name: Draft review

outcomes.name: needs your picks
outcomes.when: The findings are listed and the person hasn't said which matter yet.

outcomes.name: drafted
outcomes.when: The review is drafted with the findings the person picked.

outcomes.name: failed
outcomes.when: It couldn't read the review or the change.

outcomes.name: redraft
outcomes.when: Change the draft, with a note

stages.brief:
Post the review drafted in {custom} on {issue}. Do not change files, push, or comment anywhere else.

If its verdict is `approve`, run `gh pr review --approve` with its summary as the body, and skip the rest.

Otherwise submit one review that requests changes, with the summary as its body and each inline comment on its line. `gh pr review` can't add inline comments, so write the review as JSON and send it with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews --input review.json` (put review.json outside the checkout):

```json
{"event": "REQUEST_CHANGES", "body": "<summary>", "comments": [{"path": "path/to/file.ext", "line": 42, "side": "RIGHT", "body": "<comment>"}]}
```

If GitHub rejects a comment because its line isn't in the diff, move that comment into the body under its file and line, and send the review again. Submit it once only.

Write {output}: the verdict you submitted, how many inline comments it has, and the review's link.
stages.name: Post review

outcomes.name: submitted
outcomes.when: The review is submitted on the pull request.
